newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer amid dollar strength.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer amid dollar strength.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened little changed to slightly firmer on Tuesday amid further strength in the Canadian dollar and the movement of some bond investors into the money market, dealers said.

"You can't ignore the Canadian dollar. At below C$1.38 it just seems to be getting stronger. That's certainly propelling the bills here. And also there's sentiment now, a belief that the Fed might not move," said a T-bill dealer with one bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 2.96 percent from 2.97 percent at Monday's close.

Canada's dollar opened stronger at C$1.3771 (US$0.7261) in light trading on Tuesday. Dealers said the currency's strength was based on a decline in speculation that U.S. rates will rise and expectations that the Province of Ontario will release a market-friendly budget later today.
"There are people thinking Canada can stay here (at current rate levels) for the next six months or so, maybe longer," the dealer said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.24 percent from 3.26 percent. The one-year T-bill softened to yield 3.94 percent from 3.92 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.0 percent, in the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
